text:
Morgan: ran a set of nsys captures on the 40B emulation yesterday — seeing a weird spike in a handful of kernels during KV prefetch. timeline shows lots of tiny kernels back-to-back, hard to tell which are wasting time. attaching summary below.

Kai: can you paste the top timeline snippet? are we seeing many kernel launches or a single long kernel with tiny stalls? :eyes:

Morgan: it's lots of launches. snippet: 
```
[nsys timeline] 0.00s - memcpy H2D (small)
0.003s - kernel A (softmax) 0.8ms
0.004s - kernel B (kv-prefetch) 1.2ms
0.006s - kernel C (attn-unfused) 0.6ms
... repeated per token
```

Anya: that pattern screams poor batching + kv cache mis-indexing. if prefetch is invoked per-token we spawn tiny kernels repeatedly. we should consider coalescing prefetches across sequence window.

Rene: agree. also NVTX ranges right now mark only the top-level request. we lose per-kernel attribution. suggestion: add short-span NVTX ranges around prefetch/kvcalls and kernel-selection decision. something like `NVTX:prefetch[start]` & `NVTX:kernel_choice[selector]`.

Sam: small ranges are fine but beware overhead. NVTX push/pop per kernel can add noise. we should sample on a fraction of requests or batch up synthesized ranges for low-latency traces.

Ben: alternative: emit consolidated range for prefetch group: `prefetch.group(seq_start=..., count=...)` so we don't do push/pop for each internal micro-op. that still surfaces prefetch cost without per-kernel NVTX churn.

Morgan: perf-bot ran a quick microbenchmark: enabling per-kernel NVTX increased host CPU time by ~2.8% and GPU kernel submit gap by ~0.4ms on p4d. But with per-group ranges we saw <0.3% overhead.

perf-bot: automated note: benchmark id 2026-03-18-004. metrics: host_cpu_ms=12.4->12.8 (+3.2%), mean_submit_gap_ms=0.9->1.3. group-range experiment host_cpu_ms=12.4->12.43 (+0.24%).

Kai: good to have numbers. proposal: instrument three things minimal: 1) request span, 2) kernel selection decision, 3) prefetch group span. keep per-kernel only in debug builds.

Anya: +1. also add tags on ranges with `selector=broadcast|shard|fallback` and `prefetch=none|partial|full` so we can pivot traces by decision. that helps correlate fallback routing with perf regressions.

Rene: naming conventions: prefer dot-delimited hierarchy `ri.request`, `ri.kernel.selector`, `ri.kvcache.prefetch_group` so Perfetto timelines fold more predictably. avoid long bracketed names.

Ben: small nit: we sometimes have multiple selector hops. include `parent_selector` tag or span parent-child relationship via NVTX correlation id. NVTX supports `nvtxRangeStartEx` with attributes -> use `correlation-id` field.

Sam: on batching heuristics: current batcher has token-window=8, we see many single-token batches in chat workloads. curious if we should keep implicit threshold at 2 tokens or use time-based coalescing (e.g., wait up to 300us).

Morgan: I tried 300us for a 1000qps sim: end-to-end p50 increased 0.6ms but throughput improved 12% and kernel launch rate dropped 38%. full logs at https://tiny.example/perf/1758324689 (internal).

Kai: sounds promising. we should add NVTX marks for `batcher.wait` and `batcher.flush_reason` with `reason=timeout|size|force`. that way perf traces show how often time-based coalescing triggers.

Anya: one more KV-specific observation: some prefetches miss because key hashing uses non-deterministic lane ordering during replication; we should add a short nvtx tag `kvcache.hash_variant` to traces to correlate misses to codepath.

Rene: agreed. also add a small numeric field `cache_hit_before_prefetch` to prefetch-group span so we can compute hit-rate delta around prefetch windows.

perf-bot: reminder: NVTX range text length influences UI readability in Perfetto; keep names <= 64 chars and tag count small. auto-trim enabled in our trace ingestion if >5 tags.

Sam: ops question: how do we persist these trace annotations for dedicated/private deployments? we can't rely on Perfetto upload. maybe stream traces to internal s3 for both hosted and private (opt-in).

Ben: for private we expose a local tracing endpoint that writes .qdump or zipped perfetto JSON — customers opt in. add config `tracing.persist=true/false`.

Morgan: plan of action: (1) implement group prefetch NVTX spans + add selector/span tags, (2) add batcher.wait NVTX around coalescing, (3) gate per-kernel NVTX behind debug flag, (4) run nsys across 3 workloads (chat, completion, bulk-embed) and compare kernel launch counts. I'll open PR with instrumentation draft and the microbenchmark harness.

Kai: please include a small example snippet in the PR showing how the span is created (C++). e.g.:
```cpp
nvtxDomainHandle_t d = nvtxDomainCreateA("redwood");
nvtxEventAttributes_t attr = {0};
attr.version = NVTX_VERSION;
attr.size = NVTX_EVENT_ATTRIB_STRUCT_SIZE;
attr.colorType = NVTX_COLOR_ARGB;
attr.color = 0xFF00AAFF;
attr.messageType = NVTX_MESSAGE_TYPE_ASCII;
attr.message.ascii = "ri.kvcache.prefetch_group:count=8;selector=broadcast";
nvtxDomainRangePushEx(d, &attr);
// do prefetches
nvtxDomainRangePop(d);
```

Anya: looks good. include example of minimal tags to avoid UI trimming. maybe `count` + `sel`.

Rene: I'll review the PR once open. also will run the 300us batching sim on our 40B harness and post numbers.

Morgan: thanks all. follow-up: I'll drop the PR link here when ready and upload the nsys captures. :thumbsup:
